name: Barnard's Star
tagline: The fastest-moving star across our sky — a dim red dwarf 6 light-years away.
history: Barnard's Star crosses our sky faster than any other star — a hand's-breadth every 175 years — because it is both close (sixth-nearest system) and moving fast relative to the Sun. The old, quiet red dwarf has been studied for a century: claimed planets have come and gone, but a confirmed sub-Earth-mass planet (Barnard b, 2024) now orbits it every 3.15 days. In about 8,000 years it will pass just 3.8 light-years away — closer than Alpha Centauri is today.
